title: Browser-Assisted Web Workflow Validation Foundation
goal: Add a first-class browser-backed web validation lane so AegisPT can test client-side, stateful, and workflow-sensitive issues that passive crawling and generic HTTP scanning do not prove.
scope: Implement a bounded Playwright-backed runner for explicitly authorized web targets and stored auth/session contexts. The first slice covers: (1) route and role-state validation visible only in the browser, (2) DOM/client-side sink observation and harmless proof markers for XSS-style validation, (3) anti-CSRF and request-origination checks on selected forms or state-changing actions, (4) localStorage/sessionStorage/token exposure and hidden-client-state review, and (5) captured evidence through screenshots, network logs, DOM snapshots, and console output. Add approval-gated run profiles for passive browser reconnaissance and guarded active browser validation. Keep the execution lane additive and reuse existing evidence, run, approval, and finding flows.
generation_reason: The project audit found that docs/testing_coverage_matrix.md still marks browser-assisted validation as planned, while OWASP WSTG explicitly includes client-side and business-logic testing. Real operator feedback also showed that green UI tests did not mean the product had browser-backed assessment truth.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Bounded browser validation only. No autonomous exploit chaining, no destructive payloads, no broad fuzzing, and no scope expansion beyond explicitly approved hosts and stored auth contexts.
notes: Reuse protected secret and session-ref flows already present in the repo.
Canonical finding schema fields must remain unchanged.
Evidence must stay replayable and operator-reviewable.

success_criteria: A first-class Playwright-backed runtime runner exists for approved web targets.
Browser-only evidence is stored through the existing artifact and finding flows.
At least one guarded browser-active profile exists without bypassing approval gates.
Client-side and workflow-sensitive checks produce evidence-backed findings or truthful no-finding output.
Tests cover stored-session use, missing-auth fallback, out-of-scope targets, and harmless proof-of-execution markers.
No destructive actions, autonomous chaining, or schema mutations are introduced.
must_not_touch: pack registry, validation, approval, deployment, or runtime binding flows

acceptance_criteria: Browser-backed runner is bounded and evidence-backed.
Missing-auth and out-of-scope cases fail truthfully.

before_promotion: The prior active task is completed and logged.
The benchmark and browser-safety boundaries are documented.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with browser-runner implementation and validation evidence.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with browser-assisted validation as implemented or still bounded.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md, or set an explicit holding state if the queue is exhausted.
